prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1441; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision you reported in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please describe where you were and what you were doing just before the collision.

A: I was driving home from work on a main road in Pasadena. Traffic had slowed down ahead of a light, so I was stopped behind a sedan.

Q: How long had you been stopped when the impact happened?

A: Maybe five or six seconds. I had just come to a full stop when I felt the jolt from behind.

Q: What happened to your vehicle after the impact?

A: It pushed my car forward into the sedan in front of me. Nothing dramatic, but enough that my head snapped back and then forward.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?

A: Only in my mirror, a second before. I didn't have time to react.

Q: Have you had any medical attention since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same evening. My neck was stiff and sore, and by the next morning I had pain running into my shoulders and a headache.

Q: Are you currently experiencing any of those symptoms?

A: Yes, the neck pain is still there, especially when I turn my head to check blind spots. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I'm trying to keep up with work, and the pain makes long days at the desk harder than they used to be.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
